title: Fronted Adverbials and Commas (KS2)
subject: English
strapline: Starting sentences in different ways — with a comma after.
facts: An adverbial is a word or phrase that tells you how, when or where something happens.
A fronted adverbial is an adverbial moved to the start of the sentence.
A fronted adverbial is followed by a comma: "Later that day, the storm arrived."
Examples of time: Suddenly, After lunch, In the morning, Without warning.
Examples of place: Beyond the hill, In the distance, Under the bridge.
Using different sentence openers makes writing flow and stops every sentence starting the same way.
Commas are also used to separate items in a list: "apples, pears, plums and grapes".

quick_quiz.q: What punctuation follows a fronted adverbial?
Is "In the dark forest" a fronted adverbial of time or place?
Add an opener: "___, the rain stopped."

teacher_tips: Collect a bank of openers children can reach for while writing.
Warn against over-use — one strong opener beats one on every line.
Show the comma is doing a job (a pause), not decoration.
